key: Agriculture & allied growth: 2023-24 FRE -1.58%, 2025-26 FAE 10.14%, 2024-25 FAE 10.70% -> ascending B, C, A.
x: Agriculture and allied grew -1.58% in 2023-24 FRE (B), 10.14% in 2025-26 FAE (C) and 10.70% in 2024-25 FAE (A), so the ascending order is B, C, A. 'B, A, C' wrongly puts 10.70% below 10.14%.
Andhra Pradesh accounts for about 75% of India's cultured-shrimp exports (SES 2025-26); it is also 1st in marine exports with a 43% share. The other percentages are not the cultured-shrimp figure.
Vision 2020 (released 1999) set first-rank targets for several products across sectors, not for agriculture, horticulture or fisheries alone, so the APPSC 2019 key answer is 'All the above'.

India is a lower-middle-income economy with per capita income of about $2,760. $2,760 is India's own per capita figure, not a World Bank threshold, India is not upper-middle-income, and $42,000 is AP's Swarna Andhra PCI target for 2047.

In the latest AP series, PCI growth was fastest at 15.26% in 2021-22 and slowest at 4.10% in 2019-20 (the SES 2024-25 series put the 2021-22 peak at 17.35%). Options A, B and C attach these rates to the wrong years.

Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act declared Polavaram a national project; it has nothing to do with Nellore's 50% green-cover target by 2047, which is a district drive (Great Green Wall, Namo Van-Nagar Van, seed balls). The other three pairs are correct.
